name: DDL row image reconstruction under concurrent DML

payload.claim: A DDL backfill or reorg path that reconstructs row or index image from concurrent KV deltas must preserve a complete reader-visible row image and full index semantics.
payload.why_high_value: Failures surface as reader corruption, missing NOT NULL column materialization, or direct data-index inconsistency.
payload.next_step: Use pinned concurrent DML windows and a strong read/admin-check oracle before widening the matrix.

payload.shape: One session runs MODIFY COLUMN that rewrites row or index image while another session performs delete/insert/update on the same key range.
minimal_matrix: reader or delete after reorg boundary
payload.strong_oracle: Row scan must not report missing NOT NULL column data; if an index is involved, ADMIN CHECK TABLE must also pass.

name: Modify-column backfill interleaved with delete or reinsert

timeline: start MODIFY COLUMN and hold at a backfill or row-rewrite boundary
issue delete on rows already seen or about to be rewritten
optionally reinsert a conflicting row image before the reader step
release DDL and validate reader/admin-check oracle
payload.hold_requirements: The harness should prove the DML landed inside the reorg window, not before setup or after terminal completion.
payload.preferred_observer: A failpoint or hook that brackets modify-column backfill writeout, plus post-DDL reader or delete statement evidence.

name: No missing NOT NULL row image after DDL reorg

payload.contract: After concurrent DML and MODIFY COLUMN reorg complete, row readers and follow-up DML must never observe a partially reconstructed row image such as a missing NOT NULL column.
red_signature: reader or DELETE reports Data is corrupted, missing data for NOT NULL column
post-DDL rowset differs across equivalent access paths
ADMIN CHECK TABLE fails when an index rewrite is part of the path
green_signature: DELETE or SELECT on touched rows succeeds
ADMIN CHECK TABLE passes when applicable
payload.notes: This oracle is direct and user-visible; no metadata-only diff should count as success.

name: Multi-artifact owner homogeneity across merge or flatten

payload.claim: When one logical operation emits temp artifacts owned by different indexes or semantic owners, every duplicate-check or merge range must preserve owner identity rather than trusting a single ambient owner.
payload.why_high_value: Violations lead directly to missed duplicate checks and ADMIN CHECK failures under concurrent DML.
payload.next_step: Prefer the smallest mixed-owner matrix: unique plus non-unique or otherwise different duplicate-check semantics in one DDL.

name: Concurrent DML during multi-schema add index

payload.shape: ALTER TABLE adds more than one index while concurrent delete and insert mutate rows between backfill and temp-index merge.
minimal_matrix: mixed unique and non-unique multi-schema change
payload.strong_oracle: ADMIN CHECK TABLE must succeed and index/table rowsets must remain equivalent across indexed and non-indexed access paths.

name: Backfill, delete or insert, then merge temp index

timeline: start multi-schema ADD INDEX and hold after temp records are produced
delete an old row and insert a new row that reuses duplicate-sensitive values
optionally add one more insert before merge
release merge and validate ADMIN CHECK plus rowset oracle
payload.hold_requirements: The harness should distinguish the pre-merge and merge phases; otherwise the case degenerates into generic concurrent DML noise.
payload.preferred_observer: A hook around beforeBackfillMerge or equivalent temp-index merge boundary.

name: ADMIN CHECK preserved across mixed temp-index owners

payload.contract: A mixed-owner temp-index merge must preserve every owner's duplicate-check semantics so that ADMIN CHECK TABLE and indexed-versus-table rowset comparison remain equal.
red_signature: ADMIN CHECK TABLE fails after multi-schema add index
unique index misses a duplicate that should have been rejected
use index and ignore index rowsets diverge on the touched values
green_signature: duplicate insert is rejected where expected
payload.notes: This oracle is intentionally consequence-first; a changed log line or task split alone is not evidence.

name: DDL modify-column row rewrite and index rewrite surface

state_model: submitter computes modify type and related index plan
owner later executes reorg, index rebuild, or row rewrite under current schema
concurrent DML can race with changing-column or temp-index rewrite windows
reader-visible corruption is possible if row image reconstruction loses a required column value
preferred_oracles: table scan or DML on touched rows
ADMIN CHECK TABLE when index rewrite participates

name: Modify-column reorg must preserve complete row image under concurrent DML

payload.p_check: The reorg/backfill path trusts that the current row image plus concurrent KV delta handling is enough to reconstruct a valid post-modify row.
payload.q_claim: Even if delete, reinsert, or update interleaves with the rewrite window, every later reader and DML sees a complete row image with required NOT NULL columns present.

boundary.before: MODIFY COLUMN is active and has entered a row-rewrite or changing-column backfill window
boundary.fault: concurrent delete or delete-plus-reinsert lands on the same logical rows
boundary.after: reader or DELETE touches the rewritten rows after the DDL boundary

payload.stop_rule: Do not call this RED unless the harness can prove the concurrent DML landed inside the active rewrite window.

trigger_condition.operation: MODIFY COLUMN with row or index rewrite
trigger_condition.phase: after rewrite/backfill starts and before terminal completion
trigger_condition.required_evidence: observer or failpoint proves the job is inside a rewrite window

payload.fault_action: DELETE touched rows, optionally reinsert a conflicting image, then allow the reorg to finish.
payload.observer_action: Run a reader or DELETE on the same logical rows and record whether a missing NOT NULL column or rowset inconsistency appears.

name: DDL add-index backfill and temp-index merge surface

state_model: backfill writes temp artifacts during concurrent DML
merge or duplicate-check later reconstructs original index state from those artifacts
multi-schema DDL can mix owners with different semantics such as unique versus non-unique
topology faults can hit while add-index is long-running and partially materialized
preferred_oracles: use index versus ignore index rowset equality
terminal DDL state under topology faults

name: Temp-index merge ranges must preserve owner identity

payload.p_check: A duplicate-check or merge task range is trusted to have one effective owner or equivalent semantics for every temp artifact inside it.
payload.q_claim: Mixed temp artifacts from unique and non-unique indexes or otherwise different duplicate-check owners cannot cause one owner's check to be skipped or misapplied.

boundary.before: multi-schema ADD INDEX has produced temp index artifacts and not yet merged them
boundary.fault: concurrent delete and insert reuse values so that different owners emit temp records into the same merge phase
boundary.after: merge or duplicate-check consumes the mixed-owner range

payload.stop_rule: Prefer a minimal mixed-owner matrix first; retire if the current implementation already splits tasks by owner before merge.

name: Mixed-owner temp-index DML window before merge

trigger_condition.operation: ALTER TABLE ... ADD UNIQUE INDEX ..., ADD INDEX ...
trigger_condition.phase: after temp records exist and before merge or duplicate-check consumes them
trigger_condition.required_evidence: hook proves the merge boundary has not been crossed yet

payload.fault_action: Delete an old row, insert a replacement that reuses duplicate-sensitive values, and optionally add one more insert before merge.
payload.observer_action: Run ADMIN CHECK TABLE and compare indexed versus non-indexed rowsets on the touched values.

name: Add-index allowed state must survive topology fault

payload.p_check: A long-running ADD INDEX trusts local scheduler, owner, and external dependency state to remain coherent across owner or PD leader handoff.
payload.q_claim: After the fault recovers, the job must finish successfully or fail in a bounded, recoverable way without leaving data-index inconsistency or an unkillable running state.

boundary.before: ADD INDEX is in active reorg or ingest
boundary.fault: owner or PD leader changes while the DDL is active
boundary.after: job reaches terminal state or remains stuck

payload.stop_rule: Do not count generic timeout noise as a bug; require direct job-state or ADMIN CHECK consequence.

name: Kill or isolate PD leader during add-index reorg

trigger_condition.operation: ADD INDEX with active reorg or ingest
trigger_condition.phase: after progress is observable and before terminal completion
trigger_condition.required_evidence: job state or logs show the reorg is active at the moment of the fault

payload.fault_action: Kill, isolate, or otherwise force PD leader or DDL owner handoff, then restore the topology.
payload.observer_action: Check terminal job state, cancelability, and ADMIN CHECK TABLE if the job reports success.

title: Severity seed: modify-column row image corruption under concurrent DML

payload.symptom: Reader or DELETE reports Data is corrupted, missing data for NOT NULL column after MODIFY COLUMN overlaps concurrent DML.
payload.repro_anchor: issue 62531 runs concurrent DML and DDL for 10-20s until reader-visible corruption appears on v8.5.2.
payload.expected_next_step: Compress the external workload into a pinned delete or delete-plus-reinsert matrix around a held modify-column backfill window, then validate the direct reader oracle before expanding.
notes: This is a direct C3 row-corruption lane, not a metadata-only drift lane.
Adjacent modify-column execution recheck bugs 61668 and 64061 are useful source neighbors but not sufficient as the primary consequence oracle.

title: Severity seed: multi-schema add-index mixed-owner temp-index merge

payload.symptom: ADMIN CHECK TABLE fails after multi-schema ADD INDEX when concurrent DML creates mixed-owner temp records before merge.
payload.repro_anchor: issue 61255 uses delete and insert during backfill plus one more insert before merge, then ADMIN CHECK TABLE fails.
payload.expected_next_step: Shrink to the smallest mixed-owner matrix, preferably unique plus non-unique, and verify whether current next-gen or classic task splitting still leaves an uncovered owner-homogeneity edge.
notes: This lane is consequence-first: the artifact or task split only matters if it produces an ADMIN CHECK or rowset failure.
Critical neighbor 60339 suggests unique-index temp-value semantics remain a fertile adjacency source.

title: Severity seed: add-index topology handoff with admin-check oracle

payload.symptom: After PD leader or owner fault during ADD INDEX, the job may succeed into data-index inconsistency or remain in a bad running state.
payload.repro_anchor: critical historical cluster includes issue59701 and several admin-check failures after kill or partition of PD leader or DDL owner during add index.
payload.expected_next_step: Use an authorized fault-capable testbed or integration harness to inject the topology fault only while reorg is active, then require terminal state plus ADMIN CHECK oracle.
notes: Keep this lane severity-admitted, but retire individual live lifts if the current environment cannot actually inject the fault or observe the active reorg window.
This is the high-severity environment lane that complements the pure source selectors.
